name: True Adam / Adam tier

lead: 'True Adam' is looksmaxxing slang for the highest imaginable attractiveness tier for men, above 'Chad' and 'Chadlite' on the community's rating scales. It describes a near-perfect face and body with no meaningful flaws.

People use the term as an ideal to measure improvement against: it shows which features, such as jaw, eyes and overall harmony, they are trying to approach through grooming, fitness and procedures. Members debate whether any real person qualifies, and some say the label is overused on social media.

paras: There is no procedure for becoming one. Members start threads asking whether a person is Adam-tier, compare celebrities, and discuss the ideal jaw or facial archetype for maximum appeal. Some project-style threads treat it as a long-term improvement target.
The term is subjective and sets an ideal that most people will not reach, which some members themselves question. Chasing it through extreme methods carries the risks of those methods.

angle.text: The tier works as a reference ideal. Members use it to think about which traits, like jawline, eye area and harmony, would matter most when planning improvements.

lead: True Adam, also written 'Adam tier', is a term from looksmax.org and related spaces for the very top of the male attractiveness ladder, above Chad-level faces. It is used as a theoretical benchmark of a face with essentially no flaws.[1][2]

Because the term is about ideal appearance, members use it as the end of an ascension path, with threads such as 'can I ascend to true Adam' and 'project true Adam' framing it as a goal.[3][4] Others ask who has the ideal male jaw for the 'true Adam' archetype.[5]

paras: Adam tier sits above Chad on the community's rating vocabulary. In threads about real examples, users propose celebrities such as the late actor Jon-Erik Hexum as the closest candidate, while the original poster notes that a true Adam would be expected to have basically no flaws.[1] Other threads compare actors in 'true Adam battles'.[6]

Members have started threads asking whether to accept 'true Adam' as a term at all, and others question how short-form video users apply it to people they consider ordinary.[2][7] One member reports that TikTok commenters call any Chad-level person an Adam, prompting the question of who an actual example would be.[1] Further threads ask whether certain people are overrated Adams or whether a fitness-focused creator is the closest example.[8][9]

The tier appears in aspirational threads and in jokes about what traits would be needed, including height and body proportions.[3][4] It appears together with discussion of ideal jaw form for a maximal-appeal archetype.[5]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, true Adam is both an aspirational goal and a contested label.[2][1]
